paragraphs: On Sunday evening, Lily sat with Tom at the kitchen table. Teacher Kim wanted a new page for Explorers' Blog. The page showed two school days, one for Lily and one for Tom. "What time do you get up?" she asked. "I get up at a quarter past six," said Tom. "Then I have breakfast, and I take the bus to school with Ben." "I get up at six," said Lily, "because I feed Pip first." Pip slept under the table.

"What is your first lesson?" asked Lily. "On Monday, I have history," said Tom. "We learn about the old town and the people who lived there." "I like it, because the stories are interesting." "My first lesson is English at half past eight," said Lily. "I am never late." "I have been late only once," said Tom. "The bus was very slow that morning." "Have you ever forgotten your bag?" asked Lily. "Yes, twice," said Tom, and he laughed. "Mom brought it to school both times."

"What do you do after school?" asked Lily. "I play football with Ben on Tuesday and Friday," said Tom. "I do my homework before dinner." Lily pointed at the calendar on the wall. "Every Tuesday and Friday has a red circle," she said. "That is football," said Tom. "The green circle on Thursday is for your club." "Yes, we meet in the library after lunch," said Lily.

Lily turned to a new page. "Teacher Kim also asks about spring and summer," she said. "We have no spring in Thailand," said Tom. "I know," said Lily. "I have read about spring in my English book, but I have never seen it." "What do you do in summer?" "Summer is hot, and school is closed," said Tom. "We go to Green Hill, and Grandpa takes us fishing." "I help Grandma in the kitchen," said Lily. She wrote "no spring" on her page and drew a small flower.

Lily read the page to Tom when she finished. "You are thirteen, aren't you?" she asked. "Yes, I am," said Tom. On Monday, Teacher Kim read the page and smiled. Then Lily put it on the blog. She was happy, because her brother helped her.

sentences.text: On Sunday evening, Lily sat with Tom at the kitchen table.
Teacher Kim wanted a new page for Explorers' Blog.
The page showed two school days, one for Lily and one for Tom.
"What time do you get up?" she asked.
"I get up at a quarter past six," said Tom.
"Then I have breakfast, and I take the bus to school with Ben."
"I get up at six," said Lily, "because I feed Pip first."
Pip slept under the table.
"What is your first lesson?" asked Lily.
"On Monday, I have history," said Tom.
"We learn about the old town and the people who lived there."
"I like it, because the stories are interesting."
"My first lesson is English at half past eight," said Lily.
"I am never late."
"I have been late only once," said Tom.
"The bus was very slow that morning."
"Have you ever forgotten your bag?" asked Lily.
"Yes, twice," said Tom, and he laughed.
"Mom brought it to school both times."
"What do you do after school?" asked Lily.
"I play football with Ben on Tuesday and Friday," said Tom.
"I do my homework before dinner."
Lily pointed at the calendar on the wall.
"Every Tuesday and Friday has a red circle," she said.
"That is football," said Tom.
"The green circle on Thursday is for your club."
"Yes, we meet in the library after lunch," said Lily.
Lily turned to a new page.
"Teacher Kim also asks about spring and summer," she said.
"We have no spring in Thailand," said Tom.
"I know," said Lily. "I have read about spring in my English book, but I have never seen it."
"What do you do in summer?"
"Summer is hot, and school is closed," said Tom.
"We go to Green Hill, and Grandpa takes us fishing."
"I help Grandma in the kitchen," said Lily.
She wrote "no spring" on her page and drew a small flower.
Lily read the page to Tom when she finished.
"You are thirteen, aren't you?" she asked.
"Yes, I am," said Tom.
On Monday, Teacher Kim read the page and smiled.
Then Lily put it on the blog.
She was happy, because her brother helped her.
